report.source_text: During the TEE, the following findings were reported: ejection fraction (EF) of 40–45%; very severe aortic aneurysm (AI); dilated aortic aneurysm measuring 6.9 cm; mild mitral regurgitation (MR); minimal tricuspid regurgitation (TR); mild pulmonary insufficiency (PI); pulmonary artery pressure (PAP) of 50 mm/Hg; severe left ventricle enlargement measuring 136 cm/m2 with mild systolic dysfunction; a large (1.1 cm) semi-mobile mass on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp (NCC) mostly resembling vegetation; very severe aortic regurgitation (AR), aneurysmal aortic root (annulus, 3.1 cm; sinus of valsalva (SOV), 4.2 cm; effacement of sinotubular junction (STJ)); aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta with the proximal portion measuring 6.8 cm and the distal portion measuring 3.9 cm; a visible linear flap of aortic dissection originating about 1.3 cm after the aortic valve (AV); the dissecting flap appearing thickened and infected; and mild circumferential pericardial effusion (5 mm around all cardiac chambers).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Infective endocarditis complicated by aortic root aneurysm and aortic dissection requiring emergent Bentall surgery
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 31-year-old previously healthy male presented with fever and chills (BP 100/60, HR 100, Temp 38°C). Initial workup revealed leukocytosis (WBC 11.1 × 10³/μL), markedly elevated ESR (107 mm/hour), anemia (Hb 10 mg/dL), and negative blood cultures. Empiric broad-spectrum antibiotics (vancomycin and meropenem) were initiated. On hospital day 5, transesophageal echocardiography demonstrated a 1.1 cm semi-mobile vegetation on the arterial side of the noncoronary cusp, severe aortic regurgitation, a 6.9 cm aortic root aneurysm with aneurysmal dilation of the ascending aorta (proximal 6.8 cm), and an aortic dissection with an infected linear flap originating 1.3 cm distal to the aortic valve. Additional findings included mild pericardial effusion and reduced ejection fraction (40-45%). On hospital day 8, the patient underwent emergent Bentall procedure with replacement of the aortic valve, ascending aorta, and root using a mechanical composite graft (Carbomedics size 27). Post-operatively, he was managed in the cardiac ICU with warfarin anticoagulation, then transferred to the infectious disease ward for continued antibiotic therapy (ciprofloxacin, ampicillin/sulbactam, and vancomycin). At discharge (approximately hospital day 30), inflammatory markers had normalized (WBC 4000/μL) and INR was therapeutic at 2.6.
